laws.rule: Upper Austria's visitor tax (Ortstaxe) is EUR 2.40 per night under section 48(1) of the Oö. Tourismusgesetz 2018, rising to EUR 2.60 per night from 1 November 2026 under the state government's notice LGBl. 63/2026 (about A$4.13 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026). Some Salzkammergut municipalities have a raised rate under the 6th Oö. Ortstaxen-Anhebungsverordnung (LGBl. 37/2026, in force 1 May 2026); check the ordinance for the municipality.
laws.heading: Oö. Tourismusgesetz 2018, section 48

laws.rule: Upper Austria: without a supervising person, young people may be in public places, pubs, taverns and at public events up to the end of the 14th year from 05:00 to 22:00, from 14 to 16 from 05:00 to 24:00, and from 16 without a time limit. With a supervising person, up to 16 there is no time limit (section 5 of the Oö. Jugendschutzgesetz 2001).
laws.heading: Oö. Jugendschutzgesetz 2001, section 5

laws.rule: Upper Austria: up to the end of the 16th year, buying, having and drinking alcohol is banned; from 16, spirits (also in mixed drinks) are banned. The law also bars young people from tobacco and related products, e-cigarettes, water pipes and tobacco-free nicotine products (section 8(1) and (1a) of the Oö. Jugendschutzgesetz 2001; the age band in the law's definition of young people was not read).
laws.heading: Oö. Jugendschutzgesetz 2001, section 8

laws.rule: In Upper Austria a council may, by regulation, allow camping outside campsites only in set places or on set occasions, ban it in set places, or ban it across the whole council area (section 76(1) of the Oö. Tourismusgesetz 2018). Camping is still allowed where the landowner tolerates it without aiming for a commercial gain (section 76(4)). Camping means staying beyond a short stop (more than 90 minutes in any three hours) in or next to a tent or parked vehicle (section 70(2)). Ask the council for the local regulation.
laws.heading: Oö. Tourismusgesetz 2018, sections 70 and 76

items.text: Upper Austria's youth-protection law (Oö. JSchG 2001, section 8) bans all alcohol under 16, and from 16 to 18 bans distilled drinks even when mixed or absorbed in powder. There is a vocational exception. 'Jugendliche' here means all minors under 18. Supply of alcohol by traders is dealt with under the Gewerbeordnung, not this fine band. Fines: adults up to EUR 7,000 (about A$11,123); a young person, social work and then a fine of up to EUR 200 (about A$318), or EUR 300 (about A$477) in aggravating cases. This law sunsets on 31 December 2028. The consolidated text read on 11 November 2026 includes the LGBl. 62/2026 amendment.

sources.title: Oö. Jugendschutzgesetz 2001 (Oö. JSchG 2001), Geltende Fassung vom 11.11.2026
sources.supports: section 8 youth alcohol rules, including distilled drinks even when mixed or in powder, the vocational exception, the 31 December 2028 sunset, and fine bands; trade supply sits under the GewO (read directly 2026-11-11). The consolidated text includes the LGBl. 62/2026 amendment.

psychoactive-substances.notes: These are Land youth-protection rules, not a general adult drinking age of 18 for beer or wine. They apply to visitors under 18 in this Land. Federal narcotics law is not restated here. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293. Official RIS consolidated text (Geltende Fassung) read directly on 11 November 2026.
